_note: The font FACE-SELECTION law (parity/F01-fonts.md). Given a declared family's faces and a requested weight/italic, which face renders? This is the CSS Fonts 4 weight-matching algorithm, implemented once as a pure core and run by all three renderers, because a heading that is semibold on iOS and bold on Android is the exact drift this corpus exists to prevent. The algorithm is deliberately NOT 'nearest weight': in the 400-500 band CSS searches UP to 500 first, which is why a family shipping 400+700 renders 400 for a requested 500 and 700 for a requested 501. Italic: an exact italic face always wins; requesting italic with no italic face declared SYNTHESISES (and the build warns); requesting upright when only italic exists uses the italic face rather than refusing, because a rendered wrong slant beats no text. variation[] pins axis clamping — an axis outside its declared range clamps to the bound and reports, never silently renders an extreme. fallback[] pins the chain: an unknown family is a BUILD error, but at runtime a family whose face failed to load falls back through its declared chain to the system face rather than rendering nothing.

matching.name: 400-500 band searches UP to 500 before going down
a requested 500 with only 400 and 700 takes 400, not the nearer 700
a requested 450 takes 500 over 400 (up within the band first)
in-band with nothing at or under 500 falls to the lighter face
in-band with nothing lighter goes above 500
below 400 with nothing lighter searches up
a requested 501 crosses the band boundary and goes up
above 500 with nothing heavier searches down
a single face answers every request
a single heavy face answers a light request
no faces at all is unresolvable

italic.name: upright is preferred when upright is asked for
italic requested with no italic face SYNTHESISES from the matched upright
synthesis still runs the weight algorithm first
upright requested with only italic available uses italic rather than refusing
weight matching runs WITHIN the italic set, not across it

variation.name: an axis inside its range passes through
an axis above its range clamps to the maximum and reports
an axis below its range clamps to the minimum and reports
an axis the family does not declare is dropped and reported
the boundary values themselves are inside the range
a static family ignores every axis

parse.name: axis tags are case sensitive, as OpenType defines them
a negative value survives (some axes allow it)
a malformed pair is dropped, the rest survive

features.name: an OpenType tag is exactly four characters
